creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Measured against the pinned 0.8.0 while building find-in-pane
(`corpus/herdr-0.8.0/read-depth/`, `docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md` section 17).

Two asks, one card, because the second is the fallback for the first and Muster ships
against the fallback either way.

**1. `pane.read` cannot see past a thousand rows, and cannot page.** `lines` is clamped
rather than refused - `read_terminal_snapshot` does `lines.min(1000)`
(`src/app/api_helpers.rs:120`) - so 1001, 2000 and 100000 all returned exactly 1000 rows
of a pane reporting `max_offset_from_bottom: 2978`. `PaneReadParams` has no offset or
cursor (`src/api/schema/panes.rs:252-263`), and an `offset` key sent anyway came back a
normal success carrying the identical thousand rows, since unknown parameters are
ignored. So there is no arrangement of requests that reaches row 1001.

`truncated` does come back, and it answers a different question - "there is more history
than this", true even at `lines: 80`. Useful, and not a way to detect the clamp.

The daemon is not short of the data: herdr's own `snapshot_history` reads
`recent_unwrapped_ansi(usize::MAX)` (`src/pane.rs:2651-2654`) when it writes a pane down
for durability. The whole history is there; only the API declines it.

Either a raised or configurable cap, or an offset to page with. Paging is the better
shape for a client - it bounds each response while leaving the history reachable - and
it is also the smaller change.

**2. Nothing on the API searches a pane.** No `pane.search`, no `pane.find`; `pane.read`
and the `pane.output_matched` event are the whole surface area. A daemon-side search is
the version worth wanting, because the daemon holds the buffer and because it is what
lets a client search panes it is not showing. It also sidesteps ask 1 entirely: a search
that runs where the history lives never has to move the history.

**Neither blocks Muster.** Find ships reading and matching client-side, behind a
one-function seam, and a daemon-side search replaces that function's body. What Muster
cannot do until one of these lands is see past the last thousand rows of a pane, which
the find bar says out loud rather than answering "no results" for text it never looked
at.

A third thing worth mentioning if the conversation happens, too small for its own card:
there is no absolute scroll. `terminal.scroll` is relative and `pane.scroll` is not a
method, so a client that knows which row it wants must read `offset_from_bottom` and
scroll by the difference - two round trips on two channels, and wrong if the pane prints
in between. herdr has the setter internally (`set_scroll_offset_from_bottom`), reachable
only through attach-time restoration.
title: 🔌 Upstream: a pane's history stops at a thousand rows, and nothing can search it
